Taimoor Salman

Founder. Operator. Self-starter.

I started ColorDrop in Pakistan while working full time as a graphic designer at one of the country's biggest exporters. Five years later it was shipping thousands of units a year to three countries. Now I'm back in school to build the next thing with more structure.

The decision

I left my wife behind to take this chance on a career. It was the hardest decision I've made. But no risk means no story.

Moving here meant time apart from the person closest to me, and starting over in a new country with no guarantee it would pay off. I took the leap anyway, because I'd rather bet on myself than wonder what could have happened.

About

I learn by doing.

I taught myself manufacturing, supplier negotiation, and cross-border logistics while still in school, working a full time design job and running ColorDrop's production floor in Lahore at the same time. I've carried that same "just start" mindset into every internship, class project, and side venture since, including Nishat Mills, Thousand Dimension, Innovation Nest, VOLO, and now my Master's at Temple's Fox School.

I like brands that back up ambition with real work, not just talk. That's the kind of place I want to build my career with next.

Outside of work

Six months ago I started calisthenics knowing nothing. I've already got a front lever, a move that usually takes years to learn. Same approach I use for everything: pick something hard, put in the reps, and don't wait for permission to start.
